seo.og_title: Safi Fishing Port: Boats, Catch and Seafood
seo.og_description: A living Atlantic harbour — best in the morning when boats and markets are active.

name: Fishing Port
hero_subtitle: Working harbour, boats and fresh seafood by the Atlantic.

overview.title: A working Atlantic harbour
overview.p1: Safi’s fishing port is an active harbour, not a staged attraction. Boats, nets and the day’s catch define the atmosphere.
overview.p2: Morning is the most interesting time: unloading, small-scale trade and restaurants starting to grill fish.
overview.p3: Stay on public paths, keep clear of working gear, and combine the stop with the Sea Castle nearby.

food.title: Eating at the fishing port
food.p1: This is one of the best places in Safi for simple, fresh fish.
food.li1: Grilled fish restaurants along the harbour.
food.li2: Ask what came in that morning.
food.li3: Agree roughly on price before large platters.
food.li5: Respect working areas — do not block unloading.
food.p2: A port lunch pairs perfectly with a Sea Castle walk before or after.

tips.title: Practical tips for the fishing port

1.title: Morning first
1.desc: If you care about boats and atmosphere, come early.

2.title: Stay clear of work
2.desc: Harbour staff are working; keep to public edges and paths.

3.title: Combine with the fortress
3.desc: The Sea Castle is close — do both in the same half-day.

q1.question: When is the best time?
q1.answer: Morning for boats and market energy; lunchtime for fish restaurants.

q2.question: Is the port free to visit?
q2.answer: Public quays and viewpoints are free. Stay out of restricted work zones.

q3.question: Is the fish safe to eat?
q3.answer: Busy local restaurants serving the day’s catch are the usual choice for visitors.

q4.question: Can I take photos?
q4.answer: Yes of boats and general scenes; ask before close-ups of people at work.

q5.question: How long do I need?
q5.answer: 45 to 90 minutes including a meal stop.
